name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: the parts are worth more than the group trades for
frontmatter.summary: Astra trades at Rp4,540. The sum of the parts now marks every listed stake at market - United Tractors, Astra Agro and Astra Graphia - and the unlisted divisions on the group's own-history average earnings multiple, with no double-counted debt. Auto demand is recovering and mining is not. Buy.
thesis: Cheap on its own history: the group trades on 5.6x FY2025 earnings and 0.8x of book, against own-history averages of 7.2x and 1.1x [S0].

Our look-through sum-of-the-parts marks the parts at Rp4,250 after holding the discount at 25%; the price itself implies a discount of 19.9% to the same marks, so we hold the discount slightly wider than the market, not narrower.
The blended target embeds only a partial narrowing - the P/E and P/BV cross-checks carry no discount at all - and that is the honest framing of this thesis rather than a claim the discount closes.

Capital return is now dated and funded: IDR8.00tn of buyback was authorised on 17 July 2026 to run to 16 July 2027, and the prior IDR7.40tn programme was completed, so the base case carries execution rather than assuming it away [S8, S2].
The bear case is the discount widening within its persistent range while mining stays weak, financing credit costs rise and the joint-venture income falls; it is carried explicitly at Rp5,009.

catalysts.event: FY2026 audited results and final dividend proposal
End of the buyback window approved at the July extraordinary meeting

frontmatter.catalyst_note: named and dated discount catalyst: execution of the authorised buyback window to 16 July 2027 at holdco level, alongside the May-2026 capital-allocation roadmap [S8, S11]

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of Astra International with a **BUY** rating and a twelve-month target of Rp5,344 against a price of Rp4,540, an expected total return of 26.4% including the Rp393 of dividends we expect to be paid inside the window. That is a 17.7% price return plus the dividend, and it rests on two observations rather than on a story about the controlling shareholder [S6].

The first is that the market is valuing the group as one declining business while its largest and most profitable halves are growing. In the first half of 2026 the automotive business earned more than in the same half a year earlier and the financial services business grew again, while the mining and heavy-equipment arm nearly halved; the group now reports three core businesses precisely because those three earn about nine tenths of group profit [S2, S3]. National car demand, which fell through 2025, is recovering strongly [S4, S7]. The heavy-equipment and coal-linked downturn is real, but it is a part of the group we can size, not the whole of it.

The second is that the marks are now the marks the market can see. Our sum-of-the-parts puts every listed stake in at its traded market value, with the ownership percentage taken from the audited subsidiary list [S6]. The listed stakes are United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari and Astra Graphia; the unlisted divisions are marked on the group's own-history average earnings multiple from our data pack, the only dated trading history we hold for them [S0, S6]. No holding-company net debt is deducted a second time, because the marks are equity marks and each segment's debt is already inside its own earnings [S5]. We then apply the holdco discount the method card makes the base rate, 25%, which is wider than the 19.9% the traded price itself implies [S2, S4]. On that construction the parts are worth Rp4,250 and the primary method carries 60% of the weight.

The cross-checks sit above that, and we say so plainly: the group's own-history average multiples put the same earnings stream at Rp5,911 and the same book at Rp6,423 [S0], and those methods carry no discount at all, so the blended target embeds a discount materially narrower than the 25% we hold on the sum of the parts. That partial narrowing is the honest description of this thesis. At Rp4,540 the market is paying 5.6x FY2025 earnings and 0.8x book; every year-end multiple of the last four years was higher [S0].

What moves the value: the national car cycle and Astra's share of it [S4, S7]; whether the mining and heavy-equipment division stabilises as the national coal production quota resets — its H1-2026 attributable profit was IDR0.61tn against IDR9.10tn for the whole of FY2025 [S5, S4]; the financing block's credit cost [S5]; and the pace of the buyback authorised in July, which retires stock below the book value we carry [S8].

Astra International is one of Indonesia's largest listed companies: a group of more than three hundred subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates that sells, finances and services motor vehicles, distributes and contracts heavy equipment, mines coal, gold and nickel, runs toll roads, plantations, information technology and industrial property businesses, and finances a large part of all of it [S2]. Until 2026 the group reported seven divisions; from the first half of 2026 it reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as its three Core Businesses, with everything else folded into Others [S2, S3].

On the old seven-division basis, audited FY2025 net income attributable to the parent split as follows: Automotive & Mobility IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy IDR9.10tn, Agribusiness IDR1.17tn, Infrastructure IDR1.26tn, Information Technology IDR0.21tn and Property IDR0.72tn [S4]. The Automotive interest is overwhelmingly distribution and retail finance rather than manufacturing: Toyota and Daihatsu are the first and second best-selling car brands in the country, PT Astra Honda Motor is a joint venture whose motorcycles take close to four fifths of the national market, and PT Astra Otoparts supplies components [S4]. Financial Services is the group's consumer and heavy-equipment financing, insurance and life business, and the most stable earnings block [S4]. Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment is United Tractors with Pamapersada, Komatsu distribution and coal, gold and nickel mining — the group's largest earnings-volatility source [S4]. Agribusiness is Astra Agro Lestari, Infrastructure is toll roads and fleet services, and the smaller divisions are information technology solutions and industrial property [S4].

Strategy changed materially in 2026. In May the group announced a roadmap built on focus, clarity, discipline and commitment: focus on the three core businesses, a clearer framework for the wider businesses in which each must earn its place or be reallocated, a tighter capital-allocation rule with an explicit hurdle, and leadership incentives tied to total shareholder return [S11]. In July a new share buyback programme was approved by shareholders along with a management share ownership plan funded from treasury shares [S8]. Management describes the group's balance sheet as strong and its capital allocation as increasingly disciplined [S2].

Control sits with Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd, which held 50.1% of the shares at the last audited balance-sheet date and is itself part of the Jardine Matheson group [S6]. The free float is 49.0% and institutions hold 17.8% [S0]. In practice that means no unsolicited control event is available to minorities, and the capital-return path is a decision of the controller [S6, S8].

Astra began as a trading company in the late fifties and grew into a conglomerate by partnering with Japanese
industrial groups across vehicles, components and heavy machinery, then adding financial services to finance
what it sold. That partnership model still defines the group: much of its profit comes from joint ventures in
which it holds a minority economic interest but a controlling operating role, and its minority shareholders
own a share of a structure whose economics depend on those relationships continuing.

The Indonesian car market is the swing factor. National car sales fell through 2025, when the market contracted and Astra's share still reached 51.0% [S4]. They turned in 2026: national sales rose in the first half to 437,000 units, and GAIKINDO reported wholesale deliveries of 679,020 units for the first nine months of the year, ahead by about a fifth on the same period of 2025 [S2, S7]. The industry body's chairman expects the full-year target of 850,000 units to be met, helped by double-digit monthly growth in the two most recent months reported [S7]. A separate review of the market shows why the recovery is incomplete: the country last sold a million cars in 2023, the middle-income buyers who drove that year have not returned in force, and the industry's own participants describe purchasing power and access to financing as the binding constraints on volume [S9].

The heavy-equipment and mining complex is the mirror image. Komatsu unit sales fell steeply in the first half of 2026 to 1,994 units as the national coal production quota — the RKAB allocation — cut mining customers' capital spending, and the group's mining contractor volumes, its own coal sales and gold sales from Martabe all fell with it [S2]. The same division had grown equipment sales through 2025 before the quota tightening, so this is a policy-driven downturn in a business Astra controls through United Tractors [S4, S2]. Agribusiness turns on crude palm oil prices and volumes, both of which improved in FY2025 [S4]. Infrastructure earnings follow toll-road traffic and tariffs, which grew again last year [S4].

The competitive position is durable but not invulnerable. Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading car brands, the Honda motorcycle joint venture is close to a monopoly in volume terms, and the distribution and financing network is the moat: the group both sells and finances the vehicle, which raises switching costs and gives the financial services arm a captive origination channel [S2, S4]. The threat is the entry of Chinese manufacturers into the domestic market and the shift of the vehicle mix toward electrified models, which the group meets largely through Toyota's own range rather than with a proprietary platform [S9]. On the heavy-equipment side the moat is the combination of Komatsu distribution with the Pamapersada mining contractor, which is hard to replicate and is tied to the coal cycle it serves [S2].

Regulation matters more here than for most conglomerates. The mining production quota is set by the state and has already cut the group's heavy-equipment demand [S2]. The buyback itself runs under the financial services authority's rule on share repurchases by listed companies [S8]. The car market is shaped by vehicle taxes and subsidy policy, and industry participants have publicly asked for a review of the tax structure and cited past purchase-tax incentives as evidence that fiscal support moves volume [S9].

On the macro side the house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and Bank Indonesia's policy rate at 5.8, with consumer price inflation at 3.3; a consumer-durable and consumer-financing group is rate-sensitive, and the standing house regime is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand [S2, S4].

Indonesia's car market is unusually dependent on a single buyer class. Households buy most vehicles on
multi-year credit, so the market responds to interest rates, down-payment rules and consumer confidence at
least as much as to incomes, and the used-car market absorbs buyers who drop out of the new-car market.
Vehicle manufacturing is concentrated in a handful of Japanese-brand partnerships that also dominate the
component supply chain, which is why distribution networks and dealer financing relationships — rather than
factory capacity — are the main competitive assets.

Revenue has been broadly flat for four years — IDR301,379.0bn in FY2022A through IDR323,392.0bn in FY2025A, when it fell -1.5% on lower coal prices and a weaker car market [S4, S6]. Reported profit before tax in FY2025 was IDR49,288.0bn, well above EBIT of IDR38,665.0bn, and the gap is the point: the group's Honda and Toyota joint ventures are equity-accounted below the operating line, contributing IDR9.62tn of income in FY2025 [S6]. That is a permanent part of group earnings rather than a one-off, and we hold it at the last actual through the forecast. Net income attributable to the parent was IDR32,769.0bn and earnings per share Rp815 [S6].

The consolidated accounts use the direct cash-flow method, so the data pack carries no depreciation line for this filer. We restated it from the audited accounts: depreciation and amortisation of IDR17.87tn in FY2025 and IDR16.70tn in FY2024, from the expenses-by-nature note [S6]. Without that restatement the pack has no depreciation line at all and group EBITDA cannot be built, which is why the whole capital-intensive half of the group's valuation depends on reading it out of the notes. On the restated basis FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, an EBITDA margin of 17.5% [S6].

Cash generation is the group's strongest quality signal. Net cash from operating activities was IDR44.69tn in FY2025 against total net profit of IDR40,205.0bn — the consolidated figure, not the parent-attributable one, because the right denominator for a cash-flow comparison is the profit the whole consolidated group earned, including the minorities' share [S6]. On that basis cash still covered profit in FY2025 and in FY2024, which is what a financing-heavy conglomerate collecting instalment receivables should show [S6]. Two things we flag rather than clear. First, the FY2025 consolidated statements carry an unqualified audit opinion, but we did not retrieve the audit report text, so the auditor's identity and the exact opinion wording remain an open check rather than a verified item [S6]. Second, we could not re-verify the exchange's own notation page, and we make no claim about it either way [S6]. Capital expenditure was IDR17,440.0bn, and the first half of 2026 ran at roughly half of the prior-year first-half rate on a net basis [S3]. Dividends paid were IDR16,426.0bn [S0], a payout of 50.0% which the company itself describes as its policy ratio on the proposed FY2025 distribution [S4].

The balance sheet has to be read in two pieces. Group net debt is IDR56,315.0bn [S0], but almost all of it sits inside the financing subsidiaries that earn the Financial Services profit. The holding-company-relevant figure is net debt excluding those subsidiaries: IDR6.00tn at the June 2026 balance sheet, having moved from net cash a half-year earlier on the gold acquisition, the buyback and working capital [S2]. The dividend-upstream test is the one that matters for a holding company, and it passes: the parent entity received IDR18.99tn of cash dividends from subsidiaries and associates in FY2025 while paying IDR16.43tn to its own shareholders, both on the same parent-entity-only perimeter, coverage above one [S6]. The H1-2026 figure of IDR5.60tn of dividends received is on the consolidated cash-flow statement and is therefore not comparable with that pair; we quote it as a consolidated number only [S3]. Value reaches Astra's shareholders as cash actually upstreamed, and on this evidence the operating businesses are funding the parent's dividend rather than the parent borrowing to pay it.

Our forecast anchors on the FY2025 audited economics and the first-half 2026 actual. Revenue grows 1.0% to IDR326,625.9bn: the first half was down about three per cent on the prior-year half [S2], but the auto division itself grew six per cent in that half while the mining division fell fifteen [S5], and the national wholesale market ran twenty-one per cent ahead over January-September to 679,020 units against GAIKINDO's near-locked 850,000 units full-year target [S7]. The group therefore ends the year roughly flat rather than down; the earlier draft's minus-two per cent was an unsourced conservative drift we have removed. From FY2027E the growth rate is 5.0%, below the macro deck's nominal run but above the old four per cent, because the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2, S7]. Margins are held at the FY2025 audited level: gross margin of 22.1%, operating costs at 10.1% of revenue, and depreciation at 5.5% of revenue [S6] — a combination that reproduces the FY2025 EBITDA margin almost exactly, which is the discipline the base case is meant to hold. Net income attributable to the parent is IDR31,348.4bn, IDR33,759.0bn in FY2027E and IDR40,811.4bn by FY2030E. We hold the payout at 50.0% and now carry the authorised buyback as an ordinary share retirement: -2.0% in FY2027E against the IDR8.00tn window that runs to 16 July 2027, because the group completed its prior IDR7.40tn programme [S8, S2].

Earnings-quality flags, run at both levels as the method card requires. **Accruals**: clean, with cash conversion above one for two consecutive years measured against total consolidated net profit, not the parent-attributable figure alone [S6]. **Financing-book provisioning**: the financing receivables provision was increased by IDR1.16tn in the first half of 2026 while the same table shows write-offs running below the charge, so coverage is being built rather than released [S5]; this is the item a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro would stress first, and it is why the bear case shocks the group gross margin rather than only revenue. **Related-party gravity**: purchases from related parties — mainly the Honda, Toyota and Daihatsu joint ventures from which the group buys vehicles and parts — were IDR84.94tn in FY2025, close to three tenths of the combined cost of revenue, selling and administrative expenses, and sales to related parties were IDR27.94tn, close to a tenth of net revenue [S6]. These are core operating structures rather than siphon vehicles, and both amounts fell year on year, but they are large and the earnings mix depends on them. **Auditor history — open check**: an earlier draft described a 2021 change of audit firm and a return to the prior network as a lateral move; our sources contain no such record and we withdraw the claim [S6]. The auditor's identity, tenure and the exact opinion wording are open checks. **Structure flags**: we found no pledged controlling stake, no serial rights issues and no discounted placements to affiliates in the sources we hold [S6]. **IDX regime — open check**: we could not re-verify the exchange's notation page and make no claim either way [S6]. Because the auditor history is unverified rather than cleared, we carry a potential auditor down-tier as an open risk in the bear case alongside the related-party concentration [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum-of-the-parts carrying 60% of the weight, cross-checked by the group's own-history average earnings and book multiples at 25% and 15%. The cross-checks test the parts rather than replace them, and we discuss the divergence below because it is large and it is structural.

The cost of equity is 14.9% and the weighted average cost of capital 11.9%. The build is transparent: a risk-free rate of 7.4% from the ten-year government bond, less Indonesia's sovereign default spread of 1.6%, plus a levered beta of 1.36 — the industry unlevered beta of 0.90 geared for a debt-to-market-capitalisation ratio of 0.66 — applied to a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country risk premium of 2.5%. Pre-tax debt costs 9.4% and the tax rate is 22.0% [S0]. The cost of equity looks high for a name with this balance sheet because the debt in the ratio is overwhelmingly the financing subsidiaries' funding, which is the cost of doing the Financial Services business rather than leverage on the industrial earnings — worth remembering when reading the sensitivity grid, where the discount axis matters far more than the rate axis.

The primary method is a look-through sum of the parts, built in the order the holdco method card sets out. First, every listed stake goes in at market: the group owns 59.5% of United Tractors, 79.7% of Astra Agro Lestari and 76.9% of Astra Graphia, all read from the audited subsidiary list, and each is marked at its traded market capitalisation times that stake [S6]. United Tractors is not a separate division: it is the whole Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment segment, since Pamapersada, Agincourt and Acset sit inside it. Second, the divisions that are genuinely unlisted — automotive distribution and the manufacturing joint ventures, the financing block, the toll roads and Serasi Autoraya, and property — are marked on the group's own-history average earnings multiple from the data pack, which is the industry's mandated multiple source and the only dated trading history we hold for them [S0]. There is no unsourced differentiated multiple ladder left in the model: one sourced multiple for the unlisted block, market marks for the listed block. Third, no holding-company net debt is deducted, and that is deliberate: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of IDR73.05tn, of which IDR67.04tn is the financing segment's own book funding and only IDR6.00tn sits in the non-financial segments, every rupiah of it already inside the earnings we have capitalised [S5, F33, F34]. Deducting it from equity marks would count it twice. Fourth, the property division is marked on recurring earnings only: the reported FY2025 property profit of IDR0.72tn includes a IDR0.46tn one-off gain on bargain purchase on the Mega Manunggal acquisition, which we strip before applying the multiple [S6, F29].

That produces a per-share net asset value above the traded price, and the 25.0% discount we then apply is the low end of the persistent range the method card makes the base rate — wider than the 19.9% the traded price itself implies on these marks, so it is not reverse-solved to reproduce the price [S2, S4]. We hold it flat through the horizon because the card is explicit that discounts of this size persist for years and that trading below sum-of-the-parts is not by itself a thesis. The named and dated narrowing catalyst is the IDR8.00tn buyback window that runs to 16 July 2027, alongside the May-2026 capital-allocation roadmap [S8, S11]; narrowing sits in the bull case, and the base case carries the buyback as ordinary share retirement rather than as a discount event.

The cross-checks sit well above the primary method: the P/E method gives Rp5,911 on the earnings multiple and the P/BV method Rp6,423 on book, respectively 39.1% and 51.1% away from the sum-of-the-parts, both beyond the house threshold at which a divergence has to be explained. The mechanism is arithmetic — the sum-of-the-parts applies a 25% discount and the cross-checks apply none — but the consequence is not arithmetic and we will not dress it up as one: because the cross-checks carry 25% plus 15% of the weight undiscounted, the blended target embeds an effective discount far narrower than the one we hold on the parts. That is partial narrowing through the blend, and the honest statement of the thesis is that the base case is paid for by a group re-rating and by capital return, not by the discount closing in full. Readers who reject the narrowing should read the sum-of-the-parts line, Rp4,250, as the conservative case, and the cross-checks as what the same earnings are worth to a buyer who does not apply a holdco discount at all. The basis of the cross-checks also has to be named: 7.2x is Astra's own-history average earnings multiple and 1.1x the same for book, taken from the pack's own price history [S0], not a peer set and not an external estimate. The history is four year-end observations over the window our pack covers, not a full five years, and we label it as such [S0].

What today's price implies is the cleanest way to state the variant view. Solving the model for the holdco discount that reproduces Rp4,540, the market is pricing a 19.9% discount to our look-through marks [S2, S4]. That sits at the low end of the range a controlled Indonesian conglomerate normally carries and *below* the 25% we hold, which means the market is not pricing distress in the parts — it is pricing the group's earnings at 5.6x when its own four-year average is 7.2x, and its book at 0.8x against an average of 1.1x [S0]. The reverse calculation also asks what must be true for today's price to be right, and the answer is only a modest further erosion of group earnings or a materially wider discount — both of which our bear case carries explicitly rather than treats as tail risks.

**Regulatory and policy risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The national coal production quota has already cut the group's heavy-equipment demand and mining volumes [S2], and vehicle taxes and purchase-tax incentives shape the car market in both directions [S9]. Astra controls neither policy lever.

**Commodity and cycle risk — high likelihood, material impact.** Coal, gold, nickel and crude palm oil all run through the earnings: the mining division is the most volatile block in the group and agribusiness moves with the palm oil price [S4, S2]. This is the risk most likely to keep the group's multiple low for longer than our base case assumes.

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand; a consumer-durable and consumer-financing group is exposed both on the purchase decision and through the credit book [S2, S4].

**Competitive and technology risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** Chinese manufacturers have entered the domestic market and the vehicle mix is shifting toward electrified models, which the group meets largely through its Toyota partnership rather than with proprietary platforms [S9]. The auto franchise carries the top weight in the sum of the parts and, in the first-half segment disclosure, the largest share of group profit, so a share or mix loss is the single largest value risk we carry: the bear case therefore shocks the group gross margin, not only revenue [S5, S9].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block is IDR67.04tn of net debt against a receivables book and took a IDR1.16tn provision charge in the first half [S5]. It earned IDR4.64tn of attributable profit in that half, so it is both the most stable earnings block and the one most exposed to a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro; the bear case shocks the group margin for it explicitly [S5].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1% [S6]. No value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and the buyback mechanically raises the controller's proportional interest as the float shrinks; the discount can widen while holders wait, and waiting is not a catalyst. This is the risk our rating is most exposed to, and it is why the base case holds the discount flat instead of narrowing it.
**Liquidity risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR232.7bn a day on average with no zero-volume days in the last quarter, so the name is large and liquid for any position this book could take [S0].

**Dividend risk — low to medium.** The parent received more in dividends from its subsidiaries and associates than it paid to its own shareholders in FY2025 [S6], and the FY2026 interim was declared at the prior year's level despite the profit decline, which is a deliberate signal of intent [S10]. A deeper mining downturn that cut upstream distributions would put the payout under pressure.

The base case (50%) already contains the near-locked part of the car recovery: the industry target of 850,000 units needs only the fourth-quarter run-rate to keep pace with the January-September average, and Astra's 51.0% share of the market is assumed to hold, so the group grows revenue 1.0% this year and 5.0% thereafter, holds the discount at 25% and carries the authorised buyback through share retirement; it gives Rp5,344. The bull case (25%) is reserved for the genuinely uncertain upside: Astra taking share from the Chinese and electrified entrants rather than losing it, a richer vehicle mix and hence a better auto margin, the gold ramp and the wider-business reallocation under the May-2026 roadmap adding earnings, and the buyback plus the new capital-allocation framework narrowing the discount materially toward the low end of its persistent range; it values the shares at Rp5,677. The bear case (25%) assumes coal and palm oil weaken further, the quota keeps heavy-equipment demand depressed — the mining segment's attributable profit already fell to IDR0.61tn in the first half from IDR9.10tn for the whole of FY2025 — that financing credit costs rise against a rate-sensitive macro, that the joint-venture income falls, and that the discount widens within its persistent range while the buyback fails to close it; it values the shares at Rp5,009. The shocks are mirrored: the discount moves by the same number of points in each direction, revenue growth by the same magnitude, the gross margin by the same magnitude, and the joint-venture contribution by the same amount, so the spread comes from the parts rather than from a stacked bear case.

Holding-company discounts are one of the most persistent anomalies in equity markets: a parent that controls
listed or operating subsidiaries frequently trades below the value of its stake in them, and the gap often
survives for years because closing it requires a decision the controller is not obliged to make. Minority
holders who buy the discount are therefore paid in dividends and buybacks while they wait, and are exposed to
the discount widening rather than to the businesses failing.

Signposts that would change our view: a monthly wholesale run-rate consistent with the industry target while Astra's share holds [S7]; Komatsu and mining-contractor volumes stabilising in the quarterly releases against a reset quota [S2]; capital-allocation action on the underperforming wider businesses under the new framework [S11]; disclosure of buyback execution against the authorised amount [S8]; and any deterioration in the parent's upstream dividend coverage from its comfortable FY2025 position [S6].

Ownership is concentrated and stable. Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd held 50.1% of the issued shares at the last audited date and is part of the Jardine Matheson group; the free float is 49.0% and institutions hold 17.8% [S6, S0]. No pledged controlling stake is disclosed in the audited accounts, and we found no serial rights issues or discounted placements to affiliates in the sources reviewed [S6]. The consequence of the structure is that minority holders have no route to a control event; the route to value is the dividend, the buyback and whatever the controller chooses to do with the wider businesses [S8, S11].

Related-party dealings are large and structural. Purchases from related parties were IDR84.94tn in FY2025 and sales to related parties IDR27.94tn, the counterparties being principally the Honda, Toyota and Daihatsu joint ventures from which the group buys vehicles and parts and to which it sells services [S6]. These are the operating architecture of an Indonesian automotive group rather than evidence of value leakage, and both figures fell year on year, but they are the disclosure a reader should follow [S6].

The board is led by a president commissioner with several independent commissioners drawn from the country's financial and economic establishment, and the audit committee is separately constituted [S6]. The FY2025 consolidated statements were audited under Indonesian standards [S4]; we did not retrieve the audit report text itself, so the auditor's identity and the exact opinion wording remain an open check rather than a verified item. The dividend record is one of the group's better features: total dividends per share of Rp650, Rp519, Rp406 and Rp390 across the last four financial years [S0], with an interim of Rp98 declared for FY2026 at the same level as the prior year [S10].

On ESG, the group publishes a sustainability framework with long-dated aspirations and a community programme running across the archipelago [S2]. The material exposures are the ones already in the business: the coal, palm oil and nickel operations carry the environmental and social profile of those industries, the vehicle franchise carries the transition risk of the national fleet, and the group's response to electrification runs through its Japanese partners rather than through a platform it owns [S9, S4].

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 interim dividend paid at the end of October, the monthly wholesale car data from the industry body, the FY2026 audited results and final dividend proposal expected in the spring, and the end of the buyback window approved in July [S10, S7, S4, S8]. The interim has already been declared at the prior year's level despite the profit fall, which we read as a deliberate statement about the payout's durability [S10].

Between updates we monitor five things: national car wholesales and Astra's share of them against the industry target [S7, S4]; Komatsu unit sales and mining-contractor overburden volumes for evidence that the quota-driven downturn has troughed [S2]; net debt excluding the financing subsidiaries, since a return to net cash would remove the main balance-sheet caveat on the holding-company valuation [S2]; buyback execution against the authorised amount, which retires stock below the marks we carry [S8]; and the parent entity's dividends received against dividends paid, the single most honest test of whether the holding company's distribution is funded by its operating businesses [S6].

bear.narrative: Coal and CPO prices fall further and the national RKAB quota keeps heavy-equipment demand down - H1-2026 mining solutions attributable profit already fell to Rp607bn from Rp9,095bn in FY2025 [S5, F5] - while financial-services credit costs rise: the financing book carried Rp5.4tn of stage-classified impairment provisions at June 2026 [S5] and a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro lifts arrears. The auto franchise loses share to Chinese and electrified entrants, JV income falls, and the holdco discount widens within its persistent range as the buyback fails to close it [S2, S4, S5, S8].

bull.narrative: The auto market reaches GAIKINDO's 850,000-unit target with Astra holding about half of it [S7, S4], the mining division stabilises as the quota resets, the wider-business reallocation roadmap and the gold ramp add earnings [S11, S2], share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin, and the buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount materially, to the low end of its persistent range [S8, S11].

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +1%: H1-2026 net revenue was Rp157.9tn, 3% below H1-2025 [S2], but the auto division grew 6% in H1 as the national wholesale market ran 21% ahead over January-September to 679,020 units [S5, S7] and GAIKINDO calls the 850,000-unit year achievable [S7]; the mining division's -15% H1 revenue [S5] is the offset, so the group ends roughly flat. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]; the H1-2026 mix (auto 21.1% gross margin, financial services 60.0%, mining solutions 18.0%) is [S5] and is left to work through rather than re-mixed, with the financing block's credit cost carried explicitly in the bear case rather than in the base.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, selling plus general and administrative expenses Rp32,779bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]; H1-2026 SG&A of Rp18.0tn on revenue of Rp157.9tn ran at 11.4% against 10.1% for FY2025 [S5], so the FY2025 ratio is the favourable end and we do not bank operating leverage.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, capex Rp17,440bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S0]; the group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual of Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]) - overwhelmingly the share of results of joint ventures and associates [S6, F10], chiefly the Honda and Toyota joint ventures, which are equity-accounted below EBIT. H1-2026 share of JV results was Rp5,127bn, so the FY2025 run-rate is the honest anchor [S5]. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual of 50% (cash dividends paid Rp16,426bn by the parent entity over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]); the company itself reports a 48% payout ratio for FY2025 on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4], and declared the same Rp98 interim for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -0.7% to bring the forecast share count onto the 39,920m shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 after the completed Rp7.4tn buyback [S2, S3]. FY2027E set at -2.0%: shareholders approved a further Rp8tn Astra programme at the 17 July 2026 EGM running to 16 July 2027 [S8], and the group completed the prior Rp7.4tn programme, so a second executed programme is the most likely path rather than an upside case [S2, S8].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at the low end of the 20-40% range the holdco method card makes the base rate: the marks below are earnings and market based, and the traded price implies a discount of roughly a fifth on them, so 25% is not reverse-solved to reproduce the price but held slightly wider than the market is pricing. The named, dated narrowing catalyst is the Rp8tn buyback window to 16 July 2027 plus the May-2026 capital-allocation roadmap [S8, S11]; narrowing sits in the bull case, and the base holds the discount flat as the card requires.

challenges.challenge: SOTP values all seven divisions with segment-earnings multiples, but the method card requires listed stakes at market value and unlisted parts on their own card. UNTR, AALI, Astra Graphia and MMP are listed, every holdings row uses method multiple with stake 1.0, and no market mark appears anywhere. The primary method is the wrong construction for this name.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt. The seven-division earnings ladder is gone from the primary method. Each listed stake is now a market mark: United Tractors 59.50%, Astra Agro Lestari 79.68% and Astra Graphia 76.87% of stake times traded market cap, with the stakes keyed as facts F38-F40 from the audited subsidiary list [S6], and UNTR is the whole Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment segment (Pamapersada/Agincourt/Acset inside it), so no stale segment-earnings mark survives. The genuinely unlisted blocks (auto distribution and the manufacturing JVs, the financing block, toll roads/Serasa, property) carry method multiple on sourced segment-income facts F3-F9. Per-component marks are the SOTP rows in fund record valuation.methods.sotp (UNTR 51,960, AALI 14,569, ASGR 2,468, auto 81,844, FS 64,467, infra 9,059, property 1,836; gross 226,203, nav/share 5,666). The FY2025A segment incomes are reconciled in section 1 [S4].

challenges.challenge: The only valuation input in the primary method, the differentiated 6x to 9x segment multiples, has zero evidence behind it - no segment comps, no trading history, no source in params_basis beyond the earnings facts. Financial Services at 8x P-E additionally violates the method card, which routes bank and multifinance parts through the bank card.
challenges.answer: The unsourced 6x-9x ladder is removed. Every unlisted multiple is now the group's own five-year average earnings multiple from the pack's price history (pe 7.20x, pbv 1.11x), which fund record (CONGLOMERATES multiple_source: own_history) mandates, applied to sourced segment-income facts F3-F9 [S0]. Financial Services is no longer an 8x P-E assertion: it is marked on the same sourced own-history multiple, because every financing entity in the group (Astra Sedaya Finance/ACC, FIF, Astra Life, Asuransi Astra) is unlisted and wholly or almost wholly owned [S6], so there is no listed financing comparator to run through the bank card's P/B route; the CONGLOMERATES bind is the holdco card (market-or-house for listed, a sourced segment metric for unlisted). Provisioning, segment net debt and credit-cost facts are now carried (F34, F35) and the credit cost is shocked in the bear case.

challenges.challenge: MSHE is capitalised at 6x FY2025A net income of Rp9,095bn and billed as through-cycle, yet H1-2026 MSHE fell 46pc to Rp2,704bn on the RKAB quota cut with Komatsu units down 27pc. Annualised H1 implies about Rp5.4tn, which at 6x cuts gross SOTP by about Rp22tn - roughly Rp415 per share post-discount, near 8pc of the target. FY2025A is stale, not through-cycle.
challenges.answer: The stale construction is gone: MSHE is no longer capitalised at 6x FY2025A net income. It is now the market mark on United Tractors (the whole division), so the H1-2026 collapse is priced by the market rather than by a stale segment multiple. FY2026E revenue growth is now +1% (was -2%), anchored on the 9M wholesales +21% and the GAIKINDO 850k target; quota persistence is carried in the bear case through the revenue -3pp and gross-margin -1.2pp shocks. The implied H2-2026 profit pick-up is the already-reported auto recovery [S7], with margins held flat [S6].

challenges.challenge: Property FY2025A net income of Rp719bn capitalised at 7x into the SOTP explicitly includes negative goodwill recognised on the MMP acquisition per S4. A bargain-purchase gain is a one-off, and capitalising it at 7x books roughly Rp5tn of equity value on income that will never recur.
challenges.answer: Property is now marked on recurring earnings only. The reported FY2025 property profit of Rp719bn (F9) includes a Rp464bn gain on bargain purchase on the MMP acquisition (F29, S6 Note 3a(ii), the sourced note disclosure), leaving about Rp255bn recurring; the multiple is set so 2.554x on the reported figure equals the sourced own-history 7.20138x applied to that recurring Rp255bn (value 1,836). The one-off is stripped before the mark and disclosed in section 4.

challenges.challenge: The report insists the base case holds the 25pc discount flat and needs no narrowing, yet 40pc of the blended value via the undiscounted P-E and P-BV cross-checks carries no discount at all, so the target embeds an effective discount near 15pc - narrowing through the back door. The discount is also circular, reverse-solved from the analysts own marks with the engine implying 23.63pc vs 25pc held, and the bull-case 10pc discount sits below the house 20-40pc persistent range with no 5y own-history range and no catalyst date.
challenges.answer: Reframed honestly. The summary and section 4 now state plainly that the P/E and P/BV cross-checks carry no discount, so the blended target embeds a discount narrower than the 25% held on the parts - partial narrowing through the blend, not a claim the discount closes. The narrowing catalyst is now named and dated in the frontmatter (catalyst_date 2027-07-16, the end of the buyback window) [S8]. The bull discount shock was halved to -0.10 (bull discount 15%, mirroring the bear at 35%), no longer sitting far below the card's persistent range, and the own-history label is corrected to the four year-end observations the pack covers (not five). Honest limitation: the pack holds no historical sub marks, so a full 5y discount history cannot be reconstructed - we publish the reverse-DCF implied discount (19.9%) against our held 25% instead, and say so.

challenges.challenge: P-E capitalised divisional earnings are already equity values, yet the model deducts Rp6.0tn ex-FS net debt a second time. That Rp6.0tn is group net debt excluding FS subsidiaries including UNTR, agri and other subs debt whose interest is already inside the capitalised earnings, mismatched in time against FY2025A earnings; meanwhile group net income equals the sum of the divisions, leaving zero unallocated holdco opex unexplained and none capitalised at 10x as the card requires.
challenges.answer: holdco_net_debt is now 0. The marks are equity marks (market for the listed stakes, earnings multiples for the unlisted blocks), so the segment note's net debt is already inside the capitalised earnings and deducting it again double-counts. The ex-FS stack is reconciled to S5 Note 31: consolidated net debt Rp73.05tn (F33) = Financial Services Rp67.04tn (F34) + non-financial Rp6.00tn (F11), FS identified. On holdco opex: S5 Note 31 reports the segments reconciling to consolidated net income with no disclosed unallocated holdco cost pool, so there is no sourced holdco opex to capitalise; we do not invent one.

challenges.challenge: Base holds share_change at zero beyond June 2026, meaning no execution of the authorised Rp8tn Astra plus Rp2tn UNTR buybacks, while the thesis calls capital return dated and funded. The name just completed Rp7.4tn of buybacks, so the sole named discount-narrowing catalyst is assumed not to happen and EPS and DPS carry no accretion. That is an unsourced conservative drift on the most-likely path.
challenges.answer: share_change is no longer zero beyond June 2026. FY2026E -0.7% brings the count onto the 39,920m shares outstanding after the completed Rp7.4tn programme (F36) [S2, S3]; FY2027E -2.0% carries the authorised Rp8tn Astra programme running to 16 July 2027 (F15) [S8]. The base now carries buyback execution and the resulting EPS accretion, not zero.

challenges.challenge: Post-balance-sheet handling is wrong in both directions. The declared Rp3.9tn FY2026 interim dividend payable 30 Oct 2026 and any post-June buyback execution are cash uses, yet NAV still holds the 30 June cash while DPS12 is added to the return, double-counting the dividend. And the review claims a 31 August 2026 tender-offer disclosure was filed citing S3, but S3 contains no tender or Agustus text, so the cited evidence for the search does not exist.
challenges.answer: Both directions fixed. The tender-offer sentence is retracted in fund record post_bs_review and not asserted in the report - no tender/Agustus text exists in S3 (the 1H2026 business update). On the dividend: the SOTP marks are equity/market marks with no separate parent-cash line, so the 30 June cash is not held in NAV and the declared Rp3.9tn interim (F16) [S10] is not double-counted; it is carried only in the total-return DPS12. Post-June buyback execution is carried through share_change, not as a cash double-use.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis earnings quality and 5. Scenarios
challenges.challenge: The named bear drivers of coal, CPO, quota and buyback failure never enter the model - both scenarios shock only revenue by 3pp and the discount by 15pp, with no margin, JV-income or FS credit-cost shock. FS earnings get a free pass despite a cautious rate-sensitive macro and zero provisioning, NPL or credit-cost facts, and the clean-accruals verdict compares consolidated CFO of 44.7tn to parent-only net profit of 32.8tn instead of total net profit, flattering coverage by about 12tn.
challenges.answer: Accruals now use the correct denominator: section 3 compares consolidated operating cash flow (F27) to total consolidated net profit, not the parent-attributable figure, and says so explicitly. Provisioning is now evidenced and trended: the financing book's impairment charge rose Rp1.16tn in H1-2026 (F35) with write-offs below the charge (coverage building) [S5], cited in the EQ flags and section 5 credit risk. The bear case shocks the group gross margin (-1.2pp), which carries the FS credit cost because FS revenue and costs sit in the consolidated margin; the engine's holdco scenario targets only group-level inputs, so no FS-only shock line exists.

challenges.challenge: The 850k-unit GAIKINDO target is filed as bull-case upside, yet 9M wholesales are already 679,020 units, leaving 170,980 units or about 57k per month - roughly 24pc below the 9M monthly run-rate - for Q4. That is near-locked and belongs in the base case, not the bull case. Astra holding about half is asserted without unit-share math linking 850k to group revenue, and the wider-business reallocation, MSOP alignment and new gold asset get no upside framing.
challenges.answer: The 850k target is now in the base case: section 5 says it needs only the Q4 run-rate to keep pace with the January-September average (F26), and Astra's sourced 51% share (F14) is assumed to hold. The bull case is reserved for genuinely uncertain upside - share gains against the Chinese and electrified entrants, a richer mix and better auto margin, the gold ramp and the wider-business reallocation under the May-2026 roadmap, and discount narrowing.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis EQ flags and 6. Governance
challenges.challenge: Two load-bearing clearance claims fail spot-checks. The 2021 audit-firm change and return to the prior network as a lateral large-firm move is cited to S6, but S6 contains no 2021 mention at all, so a potential auditor down-tier structure flag is asserted away without evidence. The EQ verdict leans on an audit opinion whose text was never retrieved, while claiming no special IDX notation from a page the analyst admits it could not verify.
challenges.answer: The unsourced 2021 audit-firm-change claim is withdrawn (S6 contains no 2021 mention). All three checks are downgraded to open checks in sections 3 and 6: the auditor's identity and tenure, the exact opinion wording (the FY2025 statements were audited under Indonesian standards but the report text was not retrieved), and the exchange notation status. A potential auditor down-tier is now carried as an open risk in the bear case rather than asserted away.

challenges.challenge: The auto franchise is marked at the top 8x multiple while its two stated threats - Chinese-manufacturer share gains and the electrified-mix shift met only through Toyota, plus purchasing-power and financing constraints with tax and subsidy dependence - appear only as narrative. No bear shock touches Astra market share, ASP and mix, or the near-80pc Honda motorcycle position, so the highest-multiple division carries none of the downside it faces.
challenges.answer: The auto share/mix risk is now carried explicitly: section 5 names a share or mix loss as the single largest value risk and the bear case shocks the group gross margin (-1.2pp), which sizes the economics through the consolidated margin, with Chinese entry, the electrified-mix shift met only via Toyota, purchasing power and financing constraints, and the near-monopoly Honda motorcycle position discussed [S9]. The engine's holdco template exposes no unit-share or ASP input, so the margin is the only available sizing lever.

challenges.challenge: Cross-check plumbing is sloppy in small ways that compound - the five-year own-history multiples use only four observations, the P-BV book of 230,068 is the unaudited June-2026 pack balance sheet though the 401k-char H1 LK was fetched and yields zero sourced facts, and H1 upstream is evidenced by consolidated dividends received of 5,596 against a parent-only FY2025 series, mixing perimeters.
challenges.answer: Fixed. The own-history label now reads four year-end observations, the window the pack covers, not five [S0]. The P/BV book is now keyed as a fact (bs_equity, 230,068, the H1-2026 attributable equity from the H1 LK, F37) rather than an unkeyed pack line, and the S5 balance-sheet lines used in valuation are keyed as facts (F33, F34). The H1 dividends-received figure (F13, 5,596) is stated as consolidated and explicitly not compared with the parent-only series (F12/F22); section 3 says so.

missing_bull_case.note: Base assumes zero execution of the authorised Rp8tn Astra plus Rp2tn UNTR buybacks despite a completed Rp7.4tn programme, keeps the near-locked 850k-unit GAIKINDO target in the bull case, and values nothing from the May-2026 wider-business reallocation roadmap or the new gold asset.

missing_bear_case.note: Scenarios never shock financial-services credit costs or PSAK-71 provisioning though FS is 27pc of FY2025 earnings under a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro, never shock Astra auto share against Chinese and EV entry or financing constraints, and never model quota persistence beyond a 3pp revenue haircut.

assumption_realism.note: MSHE marked on FY2025A net income after H1-2026 fell 46pc; FY2026E revenue minus 2pc then flat 4pc sits below the macro deck nominal run with no sourced reason while 9M wholesales run up 21pc; FY2026E net profit 30.6tn implies an undisclosed H2 rebound to 18.1tn vs H2-2025 17.3tn.

evidence_and_citations.note: The 6x-9x segment multiples carry no source at all; the post-BS claim of a 31 August tender-offer disclosure is absent from its cited source S3; the 2021 audit-firm change narrative cites S6 which contains no 2021 mention; F13 mixes consolidated dividends with a parent-only series.

valuation_method_fit.note: Wrong primary-method construction for a holdco - listed stakes not marked to market, bank sub on P-E not the bank card, equity-value marks with net debt deducted again, 25pc discount held only on the 60pc SOTP leg so the blend embeds about 15pc, no look-through earnings or leverage, no 5y discount history, no catalyst date.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose claims discipline while the construction is optimistic on stale mining earnings, capitalised negative goodwill, and a circular discount that reproduces the price; the divergence section mistakes arithmetic for economics while the target itself keeps 40pc undiscounted.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: House deck variables are read correctly and the CAUTIOUS rate-sensitive stance is acknowledged; the peer set is the conglomerates industry view and own-history multiples are the mandated source.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified conservatism stacks against the buy case with zero buyback accretion, flat 4pc growth below deck nominal, and frozen JV income while auto recovers, while unjustified optimism stacks the other way with trailing MSHE, a one-off property gain, and a 50pc payout vs the 48pc reported FY2025 ratio; the drifts are not mirrored and mostly unsourced.

calibration.note: Engine QC is clean with no BLOCK flags and FY-plus-1 reproduces FY2025A EBITDA margin within 0.001pp, but the EBITDA-margin calibration only tests the blended cost ratio and cannot catch the segment-mix staleness behind it.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. BUY Rp5,344 (+26.4%). SOTP rebuilt to the card - UNTR/AALI/ASGR at market, unlisted blocks on the group own-history multiple, no second net-debt deduction - at a 25% discount, with the partial narrowing through the undiscounted cross-checks disclosed rather than hidden. The buyback-window catalyst is named and dated (2027-07-16). Both round-1 FATALs rebuilt with sourced stakes and multiples; QC + judge PASS, neutral.

bias.note: Both directions audited on the current evidence. Conservative: the SOTP marks the listed stakes at already-depressed traded prices and the unlisted blocks at the group's own four-year-average multiple (pe 7.20x, pbv 1.11x), then takes a further 25% holdco discount, so the primary leg (Rp4,250) sits below the undiscounted P/E cross-check (Rp5,911) [S0]; FY2026E revenue growth is held at +1% against a 9M wholesale market +21% [S7]. Optimistic: gross margin is held at the FY2025 audited 22.1% and SG&A at the FY2025 10.1% although H1-2026 SG&A ran 11.4% [S5, S6], and the blended target carries 40% weight on P/E and P/BV cross-checks that apply no holdco discount (the house CONGLOMERATES default weights), so the blend embeds an effective discount near 12-15% versus the 25% held on the parts. The two tilts roughly offset - the SOTP leg is understated by the stacked market-mark-plus-discount construction while the blend is flattered by the undiscounted cross-checks - and sections 4-5 state the narrowing plainly rather than claiming the discount closes. Net neutral.

findings.finding: The EBITDA-margin calibration gate reproduces FY2025A within 0.001pp, but it only tests the blended cost ratio and cannot see the segment-mix staleness behind it: the mining block (FY2025 Rp9,095bn, H1-2026 Rp607bn) is now carried by the UNTR market mark, yet group gross margin is held at the FY2025 audited 22.1% [S6] while H1-2026 SG&A ran 11.4% against 10.1% for FY2025 [S5].

The blended target embeds an effective holdco discount far narrower than the 25% held on the sum of the parts because the P/E and P/BV cross-checks carry 40% of the weight undiscounted; this is the CONGLOMERATES house default weighting, not an analyst override, and sections 4-5 disclose it explicitly.

F11 non-financial net debt is keyed at 6,000 against the filing's 6,010 (S5 p.117), where consolidated 73,048 (F33) = FS 67,038 (F34) + non-financial 6,010; the 10-basis-point rounding is immaterial and does not move the bridge.

The model and packet label the own-history multiple as an "own five-year average", but the pack covers four year-end observations (n=4; mean pe 7.20x, pbv 1.11x) [S0]; the report prose already labels it four observations, so only the engine-facing label lags.
